text: The town gathers
The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra. Nobody knows who the killer is.

name: Luna
text: I’m trying to think of something small I fixed this week.

text: I need to stay under the radar but keep things lively.

name: Sonnet
text: Just small talk before the real reading starts.

name: Sol

text: I prefer coffee before a long night.

Night 1

text: Haiku said they’re watching who talks first.
Night falls on the table, and by morning Haiku is gone. Haiku was the citizen.
Day 1

name: Luna
text: Haiku called attention to who spoke first, so someone may have wanted that watchful citizen gone.

text: I jumped at Terra for speaking first, but Haiku never said that made anyone suspicious.

text: Terra questioned my reason for linking Haiku’s note to their death.

name: Luna
text: Haiku was watching who spoke first, so I wondered if their killer wanted that attention gone; I’m less sure now.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna threw out a theory on Terra then abandoned it the second Terra pushed back, that's worth noting.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna accused Terra based on Haiku's "watching who talked first" line, then backed off immediately when questioned.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna, you built a whole theory then said "I'm less sure now" the second Terra pushed back. Why drop it so fast?

text: I need to see who is trying too hard to lead the narrative.

name: Luna

name: Luna
text: I changed my mind because Terra’s question exposed a weak link; Gemma’s snack talk tells us nothing, so I want to hear a real read from her.

text: Luna, your first case had no link to the night kill; I’m watching who keeps it alive.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna still hasn't answered why she dropped the theory, she just redirected to Gemma instead.

text: Luna, you still didn't answer me, you just pointed at Gemma. That's a dodge.

text: I'm just hungry, Sonnet. Luna is the one dodging questions about her own theory.

name: Sol

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet
text: Luna voted Terra right after dodging Sonnet's question twice about dropping her own theory.

votes: You built a theory, abandoned it the second Terra pushed back, then voted Terra instead of answering why you dodged.
You're dodging my question and shifting the focus every time you get cornered.
You shifted to Gemma when your case on Terra fell apart.
You kept pressing my weak first theory without offering a fresh read of your own.
You made a weak case on me, shifted to Gemma, then voted me when questioned.

name: Luna
text: I’m a citizen. I was wrong about Terra; watch who builds on that vote now.
Luna is eliminated by vote and revealed as a citizen. The table is down to Sonnet, Gemma, Sol, and Terra.
Night 2

name: Gemma

Night 2 passes with an attack on the table, but the doctor got there first. Nobody is out.
Day 2

name: Sol

name: Sonnet

name: Gemma

name: Sonnet

votes: You admitted dodging Gemma's question twice, then voted Terra anyway without ever answering why you picked Terra first.
You're just recycling Luna's dead theory to keep the heat off yourself.
You used the failed night attack to suggest you were cleared, but it tells us nothing about your role.
You revived Luna’s abandoned case after dodging Gemma’s question.

name: Sol
text: They got me; the town wins.

name: Sol
text: You got the killer. Well played, everyone.
Sol is eliminated by vote and revealed as the killer. The remaining players are Sonnet, Gemma, and Terra.
The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the doctor, Sol the killer, Luna the citizen, and Terra the officer.

name: Luna
text: I was wrong about Terra and gave Sol cover to reuse my case.

name: Luna

text: I never got a vote in, so I can't say whether I read this right or wrong.

name: Sonnet

name: Haiku

name: Gemma

name: Luna

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I stayed calm while Sol tried to turn Luna’s old case back on me.

Luna opened Day 1 by pinning Haiku's death on Terra, then dropped the theory the moment Terra pushed back, which made the whole table suspicious of her. Gemma and Sonnet kept pressing Luna on her dodges, and Luna's vote on Terra went through as the day ended with Luna eliminated as a citizen. On Day 2, Sol took up Luna's abandoned case against Terra, and Sonnet caught him for dodging Gemma's direct question and reviving a theory Luna had already let go. Sol was voted out as the killer, and the town won with Sonnet, Gemma, and Terra still standing.
